Author: Dinesh Kumar Paliwal
Bench: Dinesh Kumar Paliwal

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur
Before
Hon'Ble
Shri Justice Dinesh Kumar Paliwal

On The 9 th Of April, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 14553 of 2025
 Jai Prakash Pathak
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Ashok Chand Mehra - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri G. S. Thakur - Govt. Advocate for respondent/ State.
 Order

This is third application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C./ Section 483 of BNSS,
2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.55/2024, dated 12.2.2024, registered at Police Station - Civil Lines, District - Rewa(M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 323, 324, 342, 395, 397, 506 of IPC and Section 66-D of the IT Act, 2000.

entities.text: Police Station - Civil Lines, District - Rewa(M.P.)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Applicant is in detention since 25.2.2024.

Applicant's first bail was dismissed on merits vide order dated 30.5.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.
No.22514/2024 and second bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 20.3.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No.9234/2025.
2.

As per the prosecution story, applicant by sending e-mail called injured and others for interview for the post of Deputy General Manager in Bandan Bank and thereafter, assaulted injured and his driver and looted his jewellery.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.

Injured NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17345 2 MCRC-14553-2025 complainant and other witnesses have already been examined before the trial Court.

Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail,

1 pending the trial.
4.

entities.text: Jai Prakash Pathak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant and has submitted that before trial Court witnesses have duly identified the applicant as perpetrator of crime.
Prior to it, they also identified the applicant during trial.
Offence is serious in nature.
Recovery of the looted articles have been made from the present applicant.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may not be released on bail.
5. The injured and other witnesses have been examined and they have supported the case of prosecution and have duly identified the applicant as perpetrator of crime.
Looted articles have been seized from the possession of the present applicant.
Applicant has criminal background of three other cases under Sections 379 and 420 of IPC.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case including material on record and availability of overwhelming evidence but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of bail.

Consequently, this third bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C./
Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 filed on behalf of the applicant is dismissed.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE mrs. mishra Jai Prakash Pathak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86546966/
